clue.text: Group regularly boycotted Tesla

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
T is the SI symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A collective of buyers has turned its back on Elon Musk's car company.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker but is the physics unit, whose symbol is T.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a set of eight, such as eight musicians playing together.

clue.text: Spends too much on account of extra writing taking a year

indicators.note: taking means holding something inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a postscript is writing added after the letter is finished

explanation.surface: Someone splashes out because a letter's postscript ran on for a whole year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On account of' reads as part of the surface, but it is a phrase meaning 'because of', as in 'a row over money'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overpay is to hand over more money than something costs or is worth.

clue.text: Thanks — boyfriend's wrapping large picture

indicators.note: wrapping means going around something, so one piece encloses the next

parts.note: a beau is a suitor or boyfriend; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone thanks a boyfriend who is gift-wrapping a big painting.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside BEAU, just after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque scene or a group of figures arranged as in a painting.

clue.text: Event people are bound to take part in

definitions.text: Event people are bound to take part in

parts.words: Event people are bound to take part in
parts.note: surface reading: an occasion attendance at which is compulsory
setter's reading: the runners are literally tied together at the ankle in pairs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'obliged to', but here it means physically tied: pairs run with one leg strapped to a partner's, a staple of school sports days.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sports-day contest where partners hobble along with adjacent ankles strapped together.

clue.text: Case of cameo by Hitchcock inspiring one using what could be coke?

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are kept
to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the name draws the next piece inside it

explanation.surface: Hitchcock famously made cameo appearances in his own films, here apparently alongside someone on cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: Coke here is the solid fuel made from coal, not the drug or the drink; the question mark flags that coke is only one possible fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal-fired furnace or power station burns coal or a coal product such as coke for fuel.

clue.text: Assistant ref's upset with anecdote

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A match official is annoyed by an assistant's tedious story.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of ref's stands for 'is'. The letters of REF and ANECDOTE together rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A confederate is an accomplice or ally who helps someone, often secretly.

clue.text: Remains quiet after start of accusations

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the answer
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the hushing sound asking for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent once accusations begin to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: what is left after burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the residue left after something has burned, including a person's cremated remains.

clue.text: Perhaps Mark once confused grocer with funny rice

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A shopper named Mark muddled up a grocer with some odd-looking rice.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a man's name; it is the Deutschmark, Germany's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The German mark was a currency of another country, an example of money from abroad, and no longer exists.

clue.text: Authenticity is dividing field of study

indicators.note: dividing means splitting something apart, so the short word goes into the middle of the longer one

parts.note: a realm is a domain or sphere of knowledge

explanation.surface: A claim that genuineness splits an academic discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is fidelity to life as it really is, which is a kind of genuineness or truthfulness.

clue.text: Mark silver jubilee at last, showing excessive fondness

parts.note: a dot is a small mark

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: Someone marks a silver jubilee, perhaps over-sentimentally.
explanation.walkthrough: Dotage usually means senility, but it also has the older sense of doting, foolish affection.
explanation.definitionFit: To dote is to be excessively fond, and dotage is an old word for that infatuated state as well as for senility.

clue.text: Decline terms of free boob job

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so the closing letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: last letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone turns down an offer of cosmetic breast surgery at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms' suggests conditions of an offer, but here it means ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To ebb is to recede or decline, like a tide going out.

clue.text: Perhaps cowboy managed singer

explanation.surface: A cowboy apparently managed a singer's career.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher runs a cattle ranch, and a cowboy is one kind of ranch worker, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Article paper gets behind

explanation.surface: A newspaper item ends up at the back of the pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Aft is the nautical word for towards the rear of a ship, so it means at the back.

clue.text: Introduce President's first fantastic decree

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or bizarre, so the letters take an imaginative new order
first points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A president brings in an extraordinary executive order.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede something is to come before it, the way an introduction comes before the main part.

clue.text: Streaking — perhaps cock's broadcast during golf

indicators.note: during gives a little word meaning within that becomes a piece of its own
something broadcast is heard rather than read, so a word spelt differently but said the same is wanted

parts.note: a cockerel is a proud, conceited bird; the 's is 'is'
in means during, as in 'in the night'
the NATO alphabet word for G

explanation.surface: A streaker runs across a golf course while it is on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streaking' suggests running naked, but it means marking with streaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Veining is a pattern of lines or streaks, as in marble or a leaf.

clue.text: Very light infantry at the front during fighting should get send-off

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so these pieces sit inside the word that follows
at the front points to the opening letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: Soldiers leading the charge in battle are given a farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light infantry' looks like one military unit, but it splits in two: light is a light-emitting diode, and only the first letter of infantry is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A valediction is a farewell speech or act of leave-taking, a formal goodbye.

clue.text: Somehow routinely gel with setter I know only too well

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters end up in an order not given

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The setter claims to get on with someone as a matter of habit and knows it all too well.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an idiom of emphatic agreement: the speaker already knows the truth of it from experience.

clue.text: Prison block where lawyer is keeping close to Laurence Fox

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the next piece is held inside
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: to fox or throw someone is to baffle them

explanation.surface: Laurence Fox, the actor turned controversial politician, is apparently held in a cell block by a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: Fox looks like the surname of Laurence Fox, the actor turned activist, but it is a verb meaning to baffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Death row is the section of a prison housing inmates awaiting execution.

clue.text: Scrap clue for malted bun

parts.note: the answer is itself a clue, and its first word is the anagram signal that clue would use
these letters rearranged give the remaining three words of the answer

explanation.surface: A cheap piece of cake: a scrap of advice on making a malted bun.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read the answer as a clue, with ROUGH as an anagram signal applied to AND TUMBLE, and it solves to MALTED BUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a fight, and rough-and-tumble is a disorderly brawl or tussle.

clue.text: Discovered Boris intended missing an opening

indicators.note: dis-covered means with the cover taken off, so the outside letters are stripped away
missing means lacking something, so the stated letters are dropped

parts.note: your intended is the person you are engaged to

explanation.surface: Boris seemingly meant to skip the launch of something.
explanation.walkthrough: BORIS loses its outer letters to leave ORI; FIANCE loses AN to leave FICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or aperture, especially an opening into the body.

clue.text: Hippie to attend police station for hearing

indicators.note: for hearing means to be listened to, so the phrase is judged on sound, not spelling

parts.note: to attend is to be at somewhere; nick is British slang for a police station

explanation.surface: Someone from the counterculture has to turn up at the local police station for a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the nick is a police station (or prison). 'Hearing' suggests a court case; it is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatniks were the 1950s bohemian counterculture that preceded hippies, so the loose equation is fair.

clue.text: Change commercial completely

explanation.surface: An instruction to alter an advert entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust is to alter or modify something slightly.

clue.text: Shrink fleece when daughter takes son's place

indicators.note: taking someone's place means standing in for them, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: to fleece someone is to cheat them

explanation.surface: A wool fleece shrinks after a daughter takes over her brother's laundry job.
explanation.walkthrough: D replaces the S at the start of SWINDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to become steadily smaller, so it means to shrink.

clue.text: Dictator's present is fruit

indicators.note: a dictator in this sense is someone dictating, speaking words aloud for another to write down

parts.note: current means present, belonging to now

explanation.surface: A despot's gift turns out to be a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it is the adjective meaning of the moment. 'Dictator' looks like a tyrant but is someone dictating a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A currant is a small dried grape, or the berry of a ribes bush.

clue.text: Essentially unmuzzle his gun

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so the central letters of each word are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of an eight-letter word

explanation.surface: An instruction, in effect, to uncover the muzzle of a man's weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a gun whose muzzle someone is uncovering.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uzi is an Israeli submachine gun, named after its designer Uziel Gal.

clue.text: Some revolutionary gang I arrange to bring to court

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the letters are read from the end backwards
some means a part of what follows, so the answer is a run of letters inside these words

explanation.surface: A rebel band is being set up to face trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign someone is to call them before a court to answer a criminal charge.

clue.text: Rent is almost ready

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

explanation.surface: The rent is nearly due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A rip is a tear in cloth, and a rent is an old word for the same thing.

clue.text: Finally given gold and not …

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: In the end the gold was handed over and not... the sentence runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue in the surface only; the wordplay is self-contained.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor is the conjunction meaning 'and not', continuing a negative.

clue.text: … present with voucher — losing business immediately

indicators.note: losing means giving something up, so the named letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: nor with a gift voucher, when a firm is going under.
explanation.walkthrough: COUPON loses CO, leaving UPON.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereupon is a formal word for straight after that, so it means at once.

clue.text: Wife agreed to return hybrid

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way it came, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A wife has consented to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are reversed together, so W ends up last.
explanation.definitionFit: A yakow is a cross between a yak and a domestic cow, a hybrid animal.
